what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat malaria, a serious infection spread by mosquito bites. It works by killing the malaria parasite in your blood. It is not used to prevent malaria — only to treat it once you are already infected.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with food or a milk-based drink. Eating food or drinking milk helps your body absorb the medicine much better. If you cannot eat a full meal, try to have at least a few bites of food or a small glass of milk with each dose. Swallow the tablets whole with water. If you have trouble swallowing tablets, you may crush them and mix with a small amount of water and take right away. Do not skip doses and finish the full course of treatment even if you start feeling better.
dosing: The dose depends on your weight. Treatment is given as 6 doses over 3 days (at 0, 8, 24, 36, 48, and 60 hours). A typical adult dose (over 35 kg) is 4 tablets per dose for all 6 doses. Children receive fewer tablets based on their weight. Always follow the exact dosing schedule your doctor or pharmacist gave you. Set reminders so you do not miss a dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. Then continue your remaining doses on the original schedule. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and just take the next one as planned. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Contact your doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure what to do.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C and 30°C). Keep away from light and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep out of reach of children. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking this medicine with grapefruit juice, as it may affect how the medicine works. Do not take other medicines that affect your heart rhythm (such as certain antibiotics like erythromycin, antifungals, or antipsychotics) without first talking to your doctor. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or have blurred vision. Tell your doctor about ALL other medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements you are taking before starting this treatment.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience: a fast, irregular, or pounding heartbeat; fainting or feeling like you might faint; severe dizziness; serious allergic reaction (rash, swelling of face or throat, difficulty breathing); seizures; unusual bruising or bleeding; extreme tiredness or weakness; yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); or if your malaria symptoms do not improve or get worse after starting treatment.
when_it_works: Most people start to feel better within 1 to 2 days of starting treatment. You should have fewer symptoms such as fever and chills fairly quickly. However, it is very important to complete ALL 6 doses over the full 3 days even if you feel completely better. Stopping early may allow the malaria parasite to survive and come back, and the medicine may no longer work as well.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. This medicine is generally used with caution in the first trimester of pregnancy. Your doctor will weigh the risks and benefits. Breastfeeding: Small amounts of this medicine may pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while taking this medicine. Children: Dosing is based on the child's weight. Do not give adult doses to children. Elderly: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects. Talk to your doctor about any heart conditions before taking this medicine. Liver or Kidney Problems: Tell your doctor if you have liver or kidney disease, as this may affect how your body processes this medicine.
